+        # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
+        merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
+        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # int -> bytes
+        # count up the number of times every consecutive pair appears (once);
+        # afterwards the counts are updated locally around each merged occurrence
+        stats = get_stats(ids)
+        stats_get = stats.get
+        stats_values = stats.values()
+        for i in range(num_merges):
+            # find the pair with the highest count; ties go to the pair whose
+            # first occurrence in ids is earliest, which is what max() over a
+            # freshly recounted dict (insertion = first-seen order) would pick
+            pair = max(stats, key=stats_get)
+            top = stats[pair]
+            if list(stats_values).count(top) > 1:
+                cands = {p for p, c in stats.items() if c == top}
+                for p in zip(ids, ids[1:]):
+                    if p in cands:
+                        pair = p
+                        break
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+            new = merge(ids, pair, idx)
+            _update_stats(stats, ids, new, pair, idx)
+            ids = new
+            # save the merge
+            merges[pair] = idx
+            vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]
+            # prints
+            if verbose:
+                print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")

actions.reason: BasicTokenizer.train used to recount every pair over the whole sequence on each merge. Now it counts once and then, after each merge, updates the counts only around the merged occurrences, and drops pairs whose count reaches zero. Ties still go to the pair that first appears earliest in ids, which is the pair max() picks from a fresh get_stats dict, so the merges are identical. Evaluated: equivalence identical, train_ir ratio 0.847.
